title: Stores: writable, readable, derived — and when a rune is enough

videos.script:
Before runes, Svelte shared state with stores. {{before}} A store is any object with a subscribe method, and most Svelte code written before this year is full of them.

So you build one by hand. {{hand}} A clock, in eight lines, and the dollar sign that subscribes a component to it.

Then the three functions that build stores properly. {{three}} Writable, readable and derived, assembled into a small study timer.

Then the modern way. {{class}} The planner's state moves out of its component and into a class, with state and derived fields. It reads like ordinary JavaScript, and lesson nineteen will test it without a browser.

And last, the choice. {{choice}} Runes for the state your application owns. Stores for values that arrive from outside over time. And one trap both share: a single instance exported from a module, which on a server belongs to every visitor at once.
